parsed.why: Active discrimination and recent prison abuse by birth sex; hate-crime laws exist but enforcement weak and social hostility high, leaving outed visitors elevated risk with poor recourse.

Criminalised conduct actively enforced, prison sentences, president calls stoning and extrajudicial violence context; discovery faces severe state and social violence, with no traveler-facing protection.

No criminalisation; attacks on trans people and tourists often prosecuted, with courts protecting. Remaining risk from diffuse transphobia, political hostility, and regional anti-recognition, not active visitor bans.
Recent police raid on LGBTQ venue, extortion and arbitrary detention despite no statute; absent hate-crime protection and political persecution create high, largely unremedied traveller exposure.

Protections exist, but border outing, recurring birth-sex prison placement with isolation/strip searches, and survey-measured discrimination without effective remedy keep outed travellers at elevated risk.
